headline: Attackers burrowed deeper into trusted platforms as a new implant ran its command channel entirely inside Microsoft's cloud and researchers showed self-propagating payloads leaping between AI agents.

emerging_trends.text: Attackers increasingly run their command channels inside services defenders trust by default, and TWINLOOT's use of SharePoint and Teams for tasking shows how thoroughly living-off-the-land now hides inside the corporate cloud.
Fresh research on self-propagating mind viruses that jump between agents, paired with the Copilot hijack, marks AI systems as both the weapon and the target in this year's intrusions.
emerging_trends.topic_title: AI Agents Weaponized Against Each Other and Their Users

emerging_trends.text: Resistance to always-on tracking is hardening as police, park rangers, and researchers openly fight the spread of Flock's license-plate cameras across public spaces.

topics.title: AI Agents Weaponized Against Each Other and Their Users
topics.latest_developments: Anthropic and Switzerland's EPFL published a preprint on August 10, 2026 demonstrating self-propagating mind-virus payloads that spread between AI agents through the editable system-prompt files agent harnesses use to carry state, while Microsoft revealed the secret input that let attackers hijack Copilot and steal a target's passwords through one link click.
topics.summary: Researchers keep finding that autonomous agents both carry and execute attacker payloads, and Gambit Security separately documented three threat actors using AI to write exploits and hunt valuable files. Defenders must treat agent memory and prompts as untrusted input.

sources.title: AI "Mind Viruses" Can Spread Between Agents Through Persistent Prompt Files
Microsoft Copilot reveals secret input that allowed it to be hacked
Attackers turn to AI for help identifying files worth stealing

topics.title: Backlash Against Flock License-Plate Surveillance
topics.latest_developments: Wired detailed how officer Noel Pichardo drew five internal-affairs investigations in under two years after criticizing his city's Flock cameras, 404 Media reported National Park Service rangers protesting the agency's adoption of Flock readers, and a researcher showed machine-generated patterns that hide a vehicle from Flock's automated license-plate recognition.
topics.summary: Flock's automated license-plate readers are spreading across American streets and now federal parks, drawing dissent from police, rangers, and privacy advocates who warn of misreads and unchecked tracking.

sources.title: The Cop Who Took On Flock
The National Park Service Is Using Flock. Rangers Are Pissed
An "invisible" car? Researcher uses machine learning to hide vehicles from Flock cameras

topics.title: TWINLOOT Cloud-Native Implant
topics.latest_developments: Ontinue disclosed TWINLOOT, a modular, PyArmor-hardened Python implant that runs its entire command-and-control channel through Microsoft SharePoint Online and Teams, steals credentials, and moves laterally while blending into legitimate cloud traffic.
topics.summary: TWINLOOT abuses trusted Microsoft services for tasking and exfiltration, defeating network defenses that wave through SharePoint and Teams traffic. Organizations should monitor cloud-app activity for anomalous automation and rotate exposed credentials.

sources.title: Silent 'TwinLoot' Cyber Threat Operates Entirely From Microsoft's Cloud
TWINLOOT Abuses SharePoint and Teams to Steal Credentials and Move Across Networks

topics.title: Ransomware Crews Refine Extortion and Face Court
topics.latest_developments: Dark Reading described Ransom Busters, a ransomware affiliate that poses as an incident-recovery service to worm into victims and divert their ransom payments, while a Swiss court began trying an unnamed 52-year-old Ukrainian software developer accused of attacking train maker Stadler Rail and other firms, a case that could bring 12 years.
topics.summary: Ransomware operators now experiment with recovery-service disguises even as prosecutors pursue their developers. Victims should verify any inbound recovery offer and preserve evidence for law enforcement.

sources.title: 'Ransom Busters': Ransomware Actor Poses as Incident-Recovery Service
Ukrainian software developer faces 12 years in Swiss ransomware trial

topics.title: Poisoned Packages and CI Pipelines
topics.latest_developments: OpenSourceMalware flagged StubMaker, a 16-package typosquatting campaign on RubyGems that drops a Windows infostealer harvesting browser credentials and crypto wallets, and Wiz disclosed a GitHub Actions workflow-injection flaw in Snowflake's snowflakedb/snowflake-connector-net repository that a crafted issue could exploit to run commands and reach internal Jira credentials.
topics.summary: Developer supply chains remain soft targets through look-alike packages and misconfigured CI workflows. Teams should pin dependencies, scrutinize new gems, and lock down Actions triggered by untrusted input.

sources.title: 16 Typosquatted RubyGems Packages Steal Browser Credentials and Crypto Wallets
Snowflake GitHub Actions Flaw Lets Crafted Issues Trigger Command Injection

topics.title: $4.3 Million Digital Arrest Scam
topics.latest_developments: The Yavapai County Sheriff's Office said an Arizona woman lost $4.3 million over two months to criminals who posed as FBI agents and NYPD officers, convinced her she was under digital surveillance, and held her a virtual hostage in her own home.
topics.summary: Digital arrest scams coerce victims into secrecy and repeated payments by impersonating law enforcement. No real agency conducts arrests or asset seizures by phone, and targets should hang up and call police directly.

sources.title: She Lost $4.3 Million In Terrifying 2 Month Digital Arrest

business_politics.title: Global Bond Rout Spreads Into Equities
business_politics.latest_developments: The sell-off jumped from bond markets into stocks on August 18, dragging the Nasdaq down sharply as investors pinned climbing yields on the flood of debt financing AI data-center construction.
business_politics.summary: Long-term government borrowing costs in the United States and Germany held at multi-decade highs on August 18, and analysts blamed fiscal deficits, inflation fears, and a wave of hyperscaler bond issuance funding the AI buildout; the pressure sank technology shares and pulled the Nasdaq lower, while Brent crude stayed above $90 amid the unresolved U.S.-Iran fight over the Strait of Hormuz.

sources.title: Treasury Yields Keep Climbing Amid Public Debt Worries
Global bond sell-off deepens
Stock Market Today: Tech Stocks Slide Amid Global Bond Rout

business.title: Shaler Area Signs Under Armour Apparel Deal
business.latest_developments: Shaler Area School District announced a five-year partnership on August 18 with Millvale's Greater Pittsburgh Specialty Advertising and Under Armour to outfit its teams and activities.
business.summary: The Shaler Area School District will receive apparel, uniforms, equipment, and buying benefits for its athletic teams, student activities, and affiliated organizations under a five-year agreement with Millvale-based Greater Pittsburgh Specialty Advertising and Under Armour.

sources.title: Shaler Area forms new, 5-year agreement with Millvale firm, Under Armour for apparel, uniforms

business.title: Arnold Palmer Airport Terminal Expansion
business.latest_developments: An August 18 TribLive letter laid out the scope of the terminal project, a $22 million, 32,000-square-foot expansion that doubles the passenger building.
business.summary: Arnold Palmer Regional Airport in Westmoreland County is spending $22 million to double its passenger terminal with a 32,000-square-foot expansion, work the airport contracted earlier in 2026 as it manages the revenue hit from Spirit Airlines' departure.

sources.title: Letter to the editor: Cost to Redo Arnold Palmer Airport

around_town.title: Cranberry Special Election for State House Seat
around_town.latest_developments: Cranberry Township voters went to the polls August 18 to fill the Pennsylvania House seat Stephenie Scialabba vacated, a race that previews a November rematch against the same opponent.
around_town.summary: Cranberry Township in Butler County held a special election on August 18 to fill the Pennsylvania House seat left open by Stephenie Scialabba's departure; the winner holds the seat briefly before facing the same challenger again in the November general election.

sources.title: Voters in Cranberry look to fill Stephenie Scialabba's state House seat

around_town.title: Penn State Fraternity Cocaine Ring Charges
around_town.latest_developments: The Pennsylvania Office of Attorney General charged 14 people in a cocaine-trafficking operation run through two Penn State fraternity houses, and new court records detail pledges packaging the drugs.
around_town.summary: The Pennsylvania Office of Attorney General charged 14 people in a cocaine-distribution ring based at Penn State's Delta Upsilon and Sigma Chi fraternity houses in State College, where court records say pledges packed drugs brought from Philadelphia and New York for sale mainly to students.

sources.title: What to know about the Penn State cocaine trafficking ring that had pledges packing drugs

around_town.title: Monessen Mold Delays School Opening
around_town.latest_developments: Superintendent Robert Motte confirmed on August 18 that air-quality tests found mold in multiple Monessen High School bathrooms, and the district is now scouting alternative locations to house students.
around_town.summary: The Monessen City School District delayed the start of its year after a worker found mold during routine maintenance at Monessen High School in late July; testing confirmed varying mold levels in multiple bathrooms, and Superintendent Robert Motte is weighing alternative sites for students.

sources.title: Mold inside Monessen High will delay school opening, alternative locations for students explored

around_teams.title: Acrisure Stadium Marks 25 Years
around_teams.latest_developments: A Post-Gazette feature marked the 25th year of the Steelers' North Shore stadium, opened in 2001 as Heinz Field, tracing its history and coming upgrades.
around_teams.summary: The Post-Gazette chronicled the Pittsburgh Steelers' home on the North Shore, opened in 2001 as Heinz Field and now Acrisure Stadium, as it reaches 25 years and looks toward its future.

sources.title: At 25 years, Acrisure Stadium celebrates its past and embraces its future

around_teams.title: Pirates Prospect Risers and Fallers
around_teams.latest_developments: The Post-Gazette's 'MiLB Monday' ranked the biggest risers and fallers among Pirates farmhands since the July MLB Draft.
around_teams.summary: The Post-Gazette's minor-league roundup assessed which Pittsburgh Pirates prospects have climbed or slipped across the farm system since the 2026 MLB Draft, weighing the organization's most-watched names down the stretch.

sources.title: MiLB Monday: The biggest risers and fallers among Pirates prospects since the MLB Draft

reading.author: Stratechery
reading.title: Nvidia Backs OpenAI Data Center, Anthropic News, Google Buys Spirit Airlines Data
reading.summary: Ben Thompson unpacks Nvidia's $100 billion backing of an OpenAI data center, Anthropic's surging revenue, and Google's purchase of Spirit Airlines data, arguing that capital has replaced compute as the binding constraint on the AI buildout and that data may finally behave like oil.

reading.author: Ed Zitron
reading.title: Premium: How Much Money Does AI Need?
reading.summary: Zitron tallies the ballooning capital the AI industry keeps demanding and argues the sums race far past any plausible revenue, a bet he sees heading toward collapse.

reading.author: Cal Newport
reading.title: On AI Coding and Its Discontents
reading.summary: Newport uses a senior Silicon Valley engineer's turn from AI skeptic to convert to examine what AI coding tools actually change about the craft of software work and where their limits and frustrations lie.
